newsitem.title: UK: EIU sees 1.0 mln T world sugar deficit in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: EIU sees 1.0 mln T world sugar deficit in 1997/98.

text.p: World sugar production should reach 122.2 million tonnes raw value in 1997/98 and rise to 125.3 million the following season, the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) said on Tuesday.

In its "World Commodity Forecasts" report for the third quarter of 1997, the EIU said it expected global production to slip marginally behind consumption in 1997/98, leaving a deficit of 1.0 million tonnes.
The EIU's figures were based on a crop year running from September to August. The world sugar deficit was estimated at 300,000 tonnes in 1998/99, after a surplus of 1.7 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Consumption was pegged at 123.2 million tonnes for 1997/98 and 125.6 million for the following season.
The EIU report said a key factor in the first half of 1997/98 would be the stocks held by some exporters.
It singled out Brazil and to a lesser extent Thailand, which was likely to wait for higher prices in the third quarter of 1997, when Russia and China traditionally bought much of their imports.
"We expect them to be disappointed, and weak buying from these two countries to lead to a dip in prices during the second half of 1997," the EIU said.
